channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Gulf States Weigh Rare Meeting With Iran Next Week on Hormuz
item.description: A six-member bloc of Gulf states are considering meeting with Iranian officials next week to discuss the future of the Strait of Hormuz, people familiar with the matter said, in what would be the first gathering with the Islamic Republic since war erupted more than six months ago.
item.dc:creator: Fiona MacDonald and Alex Dooler

item.title: India-China Ties: How Trump’s Trade War Is Bringing Modi, Xi Closer Together
item.description: India and China share a complicated relationship. The world’s two most populous nations are outright regional rivals who fought a border war in the 1960s. Relations were severely tested more recently by border clashes in 2020 that left soldiers dead on both sides.
item.dc:creator: Alisha Sachdev and Dan Strumpf

item.title: Swedish Election Race Tightens Ahead of Sunday's Vote
item.description: As Swedish voters head to the polls on Sunday, Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson of the Moderates is seeking a second term for his center-right government in a race that has tightened sharply in the final weeks. The four-party opposition led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson has 50.7% support against 48.1% for the ruling bloc, according to the latest poll for broadcaster TV4. Charles Daly reports from Stockholm. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inflation Fears Grow as US Leads Global Bond Selloff
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Bond bears are pushing benchmark Treasury yields toward the closely-watched 5% level ahead of US inflation data that stands to determine expectations for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next week.
And Bloomberg understands that OpenAI is considering slowing down the development of cutting-edge artificial intelligence, and the ChatGPT maker’s Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman is hoping other AI companies will do the same.
Today's guests: Nataliia Lipikhina, JPMorgan Private Bank, Head of EMEA Equity Strategy; Helene Huby, The Exploration Company CEO and Founder. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: European SpaceX Rival Raises $450M to Build Rocket Engine
item.description: Helene Huby, The Exploration Company CEO and Founder, talks to Bloomberg's Daybreak Europe about raising $450 million in funding to help boost the development of Europe’s first reusable space capsule and a new rocket engine, which it says would be the largest in the region. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Political, Inflationary Risks On Europe's Horizon: Market Snapshot
item.description: The European Central Bank gathered to deliver an interest rate hike this week against a back drop of rising global bond yields, spiralling energy prices and growing political risk. Following a state election win for German's far-right AfD party in Saxony-Anhalt, attention now turns to an array of elections across multiple European countries in 2027. France in particular stand out as an area for concern for investors as the country navigates political divide and a shaky fiscal outlook. The Opening Trade spoke to guests about the biggest challenges facing European nations at a time of heavy pressure on public finances. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Far-Right Leader Roils Australian Politics With ‘Traitor’ Slur
item.description: Far-right leader Pauline Hanson has stirred fresh controversy in Australian politics after a video she posted branding a fellow lawmaker and former soldier a “traitor” prompted a volley of insults and recriminations.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: Iran and US Brace for Long War
item.description: Iran and the US are digging in for a protracted war, with little sign of a near-term ceasefire or return to normal Middle East energy flows even if hostilities remain at a low intensity. The conflict has entered a form of stalemate, with critical issues including control of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran’s nuclear program still unresolved. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jon Ronson on Men Cast Adrift
item.description: Jon Ronson’s work often focuses on unusual people and societal undercurrents. His latest book, “The Castle,” features men struggling to find purpose in a changing world. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sweden's Election Has Investors Focused on Nuclear Power, Taxes and Welfare
item.description: Voters are set to decide on Sweden’s nuclear power expansion, taxes on the wealthy and the future of the krona in Sunday’s general election
item.dc:creator: Charles Daly

item.title: Trump Rejects Warnings That AI May Lead to Human Extinction
item.description: President Donald Trump brushed aside warnings from artificial intelligence researchers that the technology is becoming too hard to control and could kill all humans, saying his paramount interest is maintaining an edge over China.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Taiwan’s No. 2 Makes Rare Italy Trip, Defying China Pressure
item.description: Taiwan’s No. 2 official is making a rare visit to Europe for a conference, a move that defies China’s push to diplomatically isolate the democratic island.
item.dc:creator: Yian Lee

item.title: Trump’s Two Days in Dallas: $5,000 Cash, ‘Socialists’ and Opera
item.description: President Donald Trump exited his midterm convention in much the same position as he entered — staring down potentially bruising November elections and facing questions about his power to influence the results.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey

item.title: Malaysia King Defers Ruling on Ex-PM Najib’s Pardon Bid
item.description: Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar has deferred a ruling on jailed former Prime Minister Najib Razak’s bid for a royal pardon, the government said in a statement on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Danial Azhar, Ram Anand and Kok Leong Chan

item.title: Korea’s Lee Faces Pushback as Trump Ups Pressure Over Hormuz
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung’s approval rating fell to a new low amid growing opposition over potential deployment of troops to the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting the political risks for the South Korean leader as he weighs options after US pressure to help secure the strategic waterway.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Katayama Calls Bessent’s ‘House’ Remark Scary in Translation
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s recent reference to himself as “the house” sounded a little frightening when translated into Japanese, while saying she understood the expression reflected the secretary’s former role as a hedge-fund manager.
item.dc:creator: Erica Yokoyama

item.title: Why India Won’t Break Up With Russia
item.description: India has spent decades balancing ties to Russia, and the USSR before it, with those to the US. Even now, amid the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine and intense pressure from Washington, New Delhi won’t let Moscow go. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UAE Pledges $46 Billion to Germany to Diversify From US
item.description: The United Arab Emirates pledged to invest €40 billion ($46 billion) in Germany in sectors ranging from artificial intelligence to energy and defense, an outlay that will deepen its ties to Europe and further diversify the Gulf nation’s trade relationships globally.
item.dc:creator: Abeer Abu Omar, Arne Delfs and Alex Dooler

item.title: Houthi-Saudi Clash Escalates as Rebels Push into Key Strait
item.description: The Houthis advanced toward Red Sea coastal areas bordering the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, as fighting between the militant group and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces intensifies.
item.dc:creator: Simon Marks

item.title: Xi’s First India Trip Since 2019 Offers Olive Branch to Modi
item.description: When Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in New Delhi this weekend for his first post-Covid visit to India, he faces the task of managing a delicate detente with his neighbor and rival.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
